rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it questions the reported expansion stage and describes subtle features (soft ICM, zona irregularity, not overly expanded) that may not be reliably supported from a single image.
Thoroughly integrates age, prior live birth, BMI, sperm quality, endometrial thickness, oocyte yield, and diagnosis uncertainty with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall logical, but there are internal inconsistencies: implantation is said to be 50-65% while live birth is at one point stated as 45-60% and even phrased as potentially higher than implantation, and euploidy wording is awkward/inaccurate.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer and caution against low-evidence add-ons; minor deviations include overconfident probability framing and some speculative counseling details.

Provides clear next steps for transfer management, luteal support, SET, lifestyle counseling, and contingency planning after failure, though some advice remains somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
